strings.name: Tiger Woods
strings.summary: Woods transformed golf’s audience and commercial reach through skill, physical preparation and competitive intensity. He won 15 men’s majors and 82 PGA Tour events. Injuries repeatedly interrupted his career; the 2019 Masters marked a major comeback. Rehabilitation plans remain distinct from confirmed tournament returns.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones; competitions, affiliations and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive match log.
strings.influence.rationale: Major and tour achievements reshaped golf’s global audience, commercial market and participation.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Majors and tour victories
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won 15 men’s majors and 82 PGA Tour events, tying Sam Snead’s tour record.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Four consecutive majors
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won all four majors consecutively across 2000 and 2001, not within one calendar year.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Recovery and training update
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Reported feeling better and training, with year-end tournament participation still uncertain.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Paused to seek treatment
strings.timeline.event-2.text: After a March car crash, announced time away for treatment and health.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Rehabilitation after crash
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Suffered serious leg injuries in a California crash, again interrupting competition.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Eighty-second PGA Tour win
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won the ZOZO Championship to tie the tour’s career victory record.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Masters comeback
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Won his fifth Masters and fifteenth major championship.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Completed the Tiger Slam
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Won the Masters to hold all four men’s major titles simultaneously.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First Masters victory
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won by twelve strokes, becoming the tournament’s youngest champion at the time.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Turned professional
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Left amateur competition and began his professional tour career.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Stanford and amateur title
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Entered Stanford University and won his first U.S. Amateur Championship.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Cypress
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Grew up in California and began learning golf as a young child.
